subject: Chemistry
source_note: Compiled from the NTA/NMC NEET UG 2026 syllabus (officially released 8 Jan 2026, based on the 2023-24 NCERT-rationalised syllabus) as reported by multiple 2025-2026 coaching/exam-tracker sources, cross-checked Sep 2026. Chemistry is grouped into Physical, Organic and Inorganic Chemistry across Class 11-12. Several full units present in the pre-2023 syllabus (States of Matter, Hydrogen, s-Block Elements, Surface Chemistry, Polymers, Chemistry in Everyday Life, Environmental Chemistry) were dropped in the rationalisation and are NOT listed here. Always verify against the current-year official NTA/NMC syllabus PDF before finalising a question bank.
exam_pattern_note: NEET UG Chemistry: 50 questions printed (Section A: 35 single-correct MCQs, compulsory; Section B: 15 single-correct MCQs, attempt any 10, best 10 scored). Single-correct MCQ format only.

subtopics: Mole concept, laws of chemical combination
Atomic and molecular mass, molar mass
Stoichiometry and stoichiometric calculations
Concentration terms (molarity, molality, mole fraction)
Discovery of electron, proton, neutron
Bohr model, atomic spectra
Quantum mechanical model, quantum numbers, orbital shapes
Aufbau principle, Pauli exclusion, Hund's rule, electronic configuration

topics.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
subtopics: Modern periodic law and long form of periodic table
Periodic trends: atomic/ionic radii, ionisation enthalpy, electron gain enthalpy, electronegativity, valence
Ionic and covalent bonding, VSEPR theory, molecular shapes
Valence bond theory, hybridisation (s, p)
Molecular orbital theory of diatomic molecules
Hydrogen bonding, dipole moment
System, surroundings, first law of thermodynamics
Enthalpy, Hess's law, enthalpies of reaction/formation/combustion
Second law: entropy, Gibbs free energy, spontaneity
Equilibrium in physical and chemical processes
Law of mass action, Kc, Kp, Le Chatelier's principle
Ionic equilibrium: acids, bases, pH, buffer solutions, solubility product
Oxidation number concept
Balancing redox reactions (oxidation-number and ion-electron methods)

topics.chapter: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
subtopics: Classification and IUPAC nomenclature of organic compounds
Electronic displacement: inductive, resonance, hyperconjugation effects
Homolytic/heterolytic fission, reaction intermediates
Purification and qualitative/quantitative elemental analysis
Alkanes: preparation, properties, conformations
Alkenes and alkynes: preparation, properties, addition reactions
Aromatic hydrocarbons: benzene structure, electrophilic substitution
Classification of solids, unit cells, packing efficiency
Point defects
Electrical and magnetic properties (qualitative)
Concentration terms, solubility, vapour pressure of solutions
Raoult's law, colligative properties
Abnormal molar mass, van't Hoff factor
Redox reactions and electrode processes
Conductance in electrolytic solutions, Kohlrausch's law
Electrochemical cells, Nernst equation, EMF
Electrolysis and Faraday's laws
Rate of a reaction, factors affecting rate
Order and molecularity, rate law, integrated rate equations
Arrhenius equation, activation energy, collision theory (elementary)
Group 15: nitrogen and phosphorus compounds
Group 16: oxygen and sulphur compounds
Group 17: halogens and interhalogens
Group 18: noble gases
Electronic configuration and general trends of transition elements
Oxidation states, colour, catalytic and magnetic properties
Lanthanoids and actinoids: general characteristics
Werner's theory, IUPAC nomenclature
Bonding: VBT and elementary crystal field theory
Isomerism in coordination compounds
Importance/applications of coordination compounds
Nomenclature, nature of C-X bond
Preparation and physical/chemical properties
SN1 and SN2 mechanisms
Nomenclature, preparation, properties and reactions of alcohols
Preparation and properties of phenols, acidic nature
Preparation and properties of ethers
Nomenclature, structure of carbonyl group
Preparation and chemical reactions of aldehydes and ketones
Preparation and properties of carboxylic acids
Nomenclature, classification, structure
Preparation and properties of amines
Diazonium salts and their importance
Carbohydrates: classification, structure
Proteins: amino acids, peptide bond, structure of proteins
Enzymes
Vitamins and nucleic acids (basic structure and function)
